evidence_quote: Petroleum in the Niger Delta is produced from sandstones and unconsolidated sands predominantly in the Agbada Formation which is the major oil-producing in the Niger Delta Complex Basin
note: Boboye & Otelaja 2013, J. Sci. Res. (Ibadan) 12:9-44. Same paper: 'Agbada Formation which is the reservoir rock in Niger delta consists of parallic sequence of sandstone and shale'.

evidence_quote: Nigeria is located inside the Pan-African Mobile Belt, a tectono-metamorphic province that was created during the Pan-African Orogeny (~600-550 Ma)
note: Adamu et al. 2026, FUDMA J. Sci. 10(4):37-44. Same paper notes several Precambrian orogenies, 'most notably the Pan-African (~600 ± 150 Ma)'; Pan-African is the dominant/last one, so no real ambiguity.

evidence_quote: the Pan-African Older Granites that intruded them along major structural zones (Rahaman, 1988; Okpoli et al., 2020)
note: Adamu et al. 2026, FUDMA J. Sci.

evidence_quote: Lead-zinc-fluorite-barite vein ore-bodies occur in the Benue Trough within the Lower Cretaceous (Albian) sequence of this intracontinental rift structure.
note: Akande, Hoffknecht & Erdtmann 1992, Geologie en Mijnbouw 71:131-144. Paper also covers Arufu/Akwana veins and the Gombe-Zurak district.

evidence_quote: outcrops in the Sokoto Basin in northwestern Nigeria, and forms the southeastern sec- tor of the lullemmeden Basin
note: Bassey & Eminue, preliminary communication on Sokoto Basin geochemistry (hrcak.srce.hr). 'lullemmeden' is the PDF's spelling.

evidence_quote: At the base is the Akata Formation, comprising pro-delta shales deposited in a deep marine, anoxic environment.
note: GEO ExPro article (trade magazine, not peer-reviewed). It confirms basal/marine/prodelta. The same page mentions detachment on an 'under-compacted, over-pressured shale sequence' but that sentence does not name the Akata. Answer is correct; overpressure not tied to Akata by name in a source I fetched.

evidence_quote: A break in sedimentation throughout southern and Central Benue Trough occurred in the Santonian times recording a period of non-deposition, erosion, folding and basic magmatism.
note: Okon, Ojong & Chikezie 2026, Global J. Geol. Sci. 24:143-157. Next sentence: Abakaliki anticlinorium formed, depocentre displaced to Afikpo Syncline and Anambra Basin.

evidence_quote: This led to the formation of the Abakaliki anticlinorium, thereby displacing the depocentre to the east and west giving rise to the Afikpo Syncline and the Anambra Basin respectively.
note: Okon et al. 2026, Global J. Geol. Sci. 24.

evidence_quote: These basal units are overlain successively by the coal measures of the Mamu Formation (Lower Coal Measures), the Ajali Sandstone (Middle Coal Measures)
note: Earth Sci. Res. J. paper on Mamu Formation coals; samples came from boreholes 'penetrating the Mamu Formation in the Anambra Basin in three Coal fields at Enugu, Ezimo and Ogboyoga'.

evidence_quote: Consists of friable, white, cross-bedded sandstones with thin beds of white mudstone near the base. Large scale cross bedding is common
note: Nigeria Stratigraphic Lexicon (ABU Zaria, 2024), Ajali Fm page: Maastrichtian; Mamu Fm page says 'Overlain by the Ajali Fm'. Minor: some papers (e.g. B12 source) call the Ajali 'Middle Coal Measures', which is not in accepted_variants. That is a grading-variant gap, not ambiguity.

evidence_quote: forming the central zone of anorogenic magmatism in Nigeria, and found a southerly decreasing age trend from early Jurassic to mid-Jurassic times.
note: Nature 259:297 (1976) abstract page, on Nigerian Younger Granite ring complexes.

evidence_quote: the exploitation of tin and Columbite initially in alluvial deposits
note: Mallo & Aluwong 2012, Continental J. Earth Sci., on tin and columbite mining at Bisichi Jenta, Jos Plateau. Text seen via WebFetch, which returns quotes as fragments; curl was blocked (403). The answer columbite is correct. The question's premise that Nigeria was a 'leading world producer' was NOT confirmed from a fetched page: the SEG abstract and USGS Minerals Yearbook pages that make this claim were 404 or 403, or rendered without text.

evidence_quote: The Kalambaina Fm type locality is exposed in the Sokoto Cement Works Quarry (Whiteman, 1982). Middle formation in the Sokoto Gr .
note: Nigeria Stratigraphic Lexicon. Age is 'middle Paleocene'; lithology 'grey-yellow and white limestone'. UDUS repository abstract also says the Kalambaina Limestone 'meets industrial-grade standards for cement'.

evidence_quote: The Asu River Group was deposited in the earliest stages of the basin formation process.
note: Okon et al. 2026, under the heading 'Asu River Group (Albian)'. The same paper calls the Abakaliki pyroclastics and Awi Fm the 'oldest deposits in the basin', but the Lexicon lists Awi Fm as a unit within the Asu River Gr in the southern Benue Trough, so the answer stands.

evidence_quote: Imo Fm conformably overlies the Nsukka Fm as one goes into the Niger Delta succession.
note: Nigeria Stratigraphic Lexicon, Nsukka Fm page. Imo Fm page gives 'Paleocene and earliest Eocene'.

evidence_quote: The Albian Bima Sandstone lies unconformably on the Precambrian Basement.
note: Nigeria Stratigraphic Lexicon, Bima Fm page. Same page: 'According to Obaje (2009), this formation was deposited under continental conditions (fluvial, deltaic, lacustrine)'. Region includes Bornu (SW Chad) Basin.

evidence_quote: Fika Fm (Fika Shale Fm) lies conformably on the Pindiga Fm and Gongila Fm
note: Nigeria Stratigraphic Lexicon, Gongila Fm page (region: Gongola Arm and its extension under Chad Basin).

evidence_quote: Age Interval: Upper Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) Province: Bida Basin- South ... sandstones and claystones interbedded with oolitic, concretionary and massive ironstone beds
note: Nigeria Stratigraphic Lexicon. The quote joins two passages from the same page (marked with '...'). 'Pisolitic' was not seen on this page.

evidence_quote: Consists of continental lacustrine sediments and the youngest Paleogene formation in the Sokoto section of the Iullemmeden Basin.
note: Nigeria Stratigraphic Lexicon. Same page: 'Equivalent to Continental Terminal Gr' (an accepted variant). Its age is debated (Eocene vs Miocene-Pliocene per other papers), but its position as the youngest unit is not.

evidence_quote: It consists of white, blue, pink clays, cross-bedded sands, carbonaceous mudstones, shales and seams of lignite (Nwajide, 2013).
note: Nigeria Stratigraphic Lexicon. Age Interval: Oligocene - Miocene; synonym 'Lignite Shales (Parkinson, 1907)'.
